what.text: This page follows refugees from Indonesia living in Papua New Guinea, as counted by UNHCR at the end of each year.
At the end of 2025, UNHCR counted 7700 Indonesian refugees in Papua New Guinea, 83.6% of all refugees from Indonesia.
Papua New Guinea is the largest host of Indonesian refugees, followed by the United States and Australia.

why.text: UCDP records armed conflict over West Papua territory in Indonesia in periods from 1976, most recently with the OPM from 2018 to 2025.
It also records armed conflicts over East Timor territory from 1975 and over Aceh territory from 1990 to 2005.

when.text: UNHCR's series for this group starts in 1978 at 1000 refugees, and the figure was at its highest, 11750, at the end of 1985.
The main years of displacement in the data are 1984 to 1999 and 2003 to 2025.

how.text: The sources don't say which routes people took or where they live in Papua New Guinea.
These are year-end totals for Papua New Guinea only, reported to UNHCR.
